newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil softer, premiums steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil softer, premiums steady.

text.p: NWE heating oil slipped a few dollars in line with losses on IPE gas oil on Tuesday but premiums were notionally steady as buyers failed to emerge.
"There is nothing happening. We thought there would be some activity today after yesterday's holiday," one broker said.
Talk on prompt and early June barges was around June IPE +$1.00-$1.50 a tonne fob Rotterdam. The only deal was 6,000 tonnes of Swiss specification May barges at June +$2 a tonne.
Traders said they still expected activity to pick up before Thursday's market and public holiday which will take most of the South and West of Germany out for a long weekend.
Benchmark IPE June gas oil futures slipped $2.25 a tonne to trade by 1200 GMT at $175.50 a tonne.
Traders said good offers of May and early June Russian cargoes should put pressure on current premiums which were pegged around June IPE +$1.50-$2.50.
One refiner was seen offering two May cargoes with at least another one unsold. A trader, holding three unsold early June cargoes said buying interest was limited.
